social.hook: My first Joe Jackson show, and I didn't go back for nine years.
social.caption: Twenty songs that night, opening with 'Steppin' Out' — and that was twenty-three years ago today. I didn't see him again until 2012.
beats: August 29, 2003. House of Blues Anaheim. My first time seeing Joe Jackson.
Twenty songs. He opened with 'Steppin' Out' and closed with 'I'm the Man'.
2003 was a full year — Peter Gabriel, The Human League, The Cure all in the same stretch.
But I didn't go back for Joe Jackson until 2012. Nine years between show one and show two.
I've seen him four times total. That first night in Anaheim started all of it.

social.hook: Four times in 25 years, and only once did they open for someone else.
social.caption: Ten years ago today I caught The Smithereens at Birchmere — my fourth time seeing them, and the only show I've ever attended there. Still the last time, so far.
beats: The Smithereens headlined Birchmere on August 26, 2016 — my fourth time seeing them across 25 years.
Three of those four were headline sets. The exception: opening for Siouxsie and the Banshees in December 1991.
Birchmere in Alexandria was new territory — the only time I've ever been inside that room.
Ten years on, it's still the last time I've seen them. That's not a complaint. It's just where the count sits.

social.hook: The English Beat opened. I had no idea I'd see them nine more times after that.
social.caption: The Human League were headlining, but The English Beat are the reason I keep thinking about this night — twenty-three years ago today. I didn't see The Human League again until 2018.
beats: The English Beat opened for The Human League at The Grove of Anaheim on August 24, 2003.
It was my first Human League show. Fifteen years would pass before I saw them again.
The English Beat were a different story — that night was number one of ten.
2003 was a dense year: Peter Gabriel, Joe Jackson, The Cure. The Human League fit right in.
The opener became the habit. The headliner took another fifteen years to return.

social.hook: 37 years between the first show and the second — and A Certain Ratio opened the first one.
social.caption: Forty-one years ago today, A Certain Ratio and the Abecedarians opened for New Order at Irvine Meadows. I didn't see New Order again until 2022.
beats: August 23, 1985. New Order at Irvine Meadows — my first time seeing them.
A Certain Ratio opened. I have never seen them since — that night is the only time.
The Abecedarians opened too. Same story: once, and only that once.
1985 was a full year — Depeche Mode, Springsteen, Tears For Fears. New Order fit right in.
I didn't see New Order again until 2022. Thirty-seven years between the first show and the second.

social.hook: The first indoor show after 18 months of nothing.
social.caption: Future Islands at House of Blues Anaheim on August 31, 2021 — my first time back inside a venue since early 2020. Five years on, I still feel what that room felt like.
beats: August 31, 2021: the first indoor concert I attended after eighteen months away from live music.
Future Islands were the band I walked back in for — a choice that made sense the moment the set started.
House of Blues Anaheim held that night differently than any room had held a show before.
Five years later, this date sits in the archive as a before-and-after line.

social.hook: The only time I ever saw George Michael perform before he was George Michael solo.
social.caption: Wham! at Hollywood Park Racetrack, August 1985 — a concert venue built inside a working racetrack, and a band still a year away from splitting.
beats: Hollywood Park was a functioning horse-racing track in Inglewood. In the summer of 1985, it was also a concert venue.
Wham! played there on August 30, 1985. I was in the crowd. The band was at the peak of what they were as a duo.
George Michael would go solo within the year. This was still before that — still Wham!, still the two of them.
41 years ago today. One show, one ticket stub, and no way to know then what it was the last of.
